title: Graphene Oxide‐Based Lamella Network for Enhanced Sound Absorption

findings.antecedent: MFGO-5 lamella structure (density 24.12 kg/m³, thickness 26 mm) vs Control-MF
findings.statement: MFGO-5 sample achieved absorption coefficient of 0.38 at 500 Hz compared to Control-MF baseline of 0.22
findings.mechanism: enhanced acoustic absorption via increased air-flow resistance and tortuosity from GO lamella blocking pores

findings.antecedent: MFGO-5 lamella structure (density 24.12 kg/m³, thickness 26 mm) vs Control-MF
findings.statement: MFGO-5 achieved 0.82 at 1000 Hz vs Control-MF 0.42

findings.antecedent: MFGO-5 lamella structure (density 24.12 kg/m³, thickness 26 mm) vs Control-MF
findings.statement: MFGO-5 achieved 0.98 at 2000 Hz vs Control-MF 0.62

findings.antecedent: MFGO-5 lamella structure (density 24.12 kg/m³, thickness 26 mm) vs Control-MF
findings.statement: MFGO-5 achieved 1.0 at 4000 Hz vs Control-MF 0.83

findings.antecedent: MFGO-5 lamella structure at constant thickness 26 ± 0.5 mm across density range 12.39-24.12 kg/m³
findings.consequent: normalized acoustic activity (128 Hz to 4000 Hz broad-band absorption)
findings.statement: Normalized acoustic activity shows nearly linear increase from ~0.48 at 12.39 kg/m³ to ~0.80 at 24.12 kg/m³
findings.quote: normalized acoustic activity based on GO loading %.
findings.mechanism: increasing GO density increases air-flow resistance and tortuosity

findings.antecedent: Increased GO density in lamella structure (MFGO-1 to MFGO-5: 12.39-24.12 kg/m³)
findings.consequent: static load carrying capacity at ~3,500x sample weight
findings.statement: MFGO-5 (density 24.12 kg/m³, 500 g sample weight) could support at least 3,500 times its own weight with negligible deformation
findings.quote: sample with a density of 24.12 kg/m³ could support at least 3,500 times its own weight (500 g)
findings.mechanism: GO reinforcement of melamine foam skeleton structure

findings.antecedent: MFGO samples compressed to 80% strain during cyclic compression test
findings.consequent: recovery of original shape after release
findings.statement: MFGO samples recovered to original shape rapidly when compressed to 80% strain, demonstrating superior elasticity compared to Control-MF
findings.quote: The recovery to their original shape was fast when compressed to a strain of 40%. The higher density samples generated superior stiffness, but lowered the recovery rate at increased compression percentage.
findings.mechanism: interconnected lamella structure provides elastic recovery

findings.antecedent: Elastic modulus of lamella structures: MFGO-1 (12.39 kg/m³) vs MFGO-3 (18.77 kg/m³) vs MFGO-5 (24.12 kg/m³)
findings.statement: Elastic modulus increased from 4.68 kPa (MFGO-1) to 7.17 kPa (MFGO-3) to 13.46 kPa (MFGO-5)

sample.population: MFGO lamella samples at 3 density levels

findings.quote: elastic modulus of the lamella structure in MFGO-1, MFGO-3 and MFGO-5 are 4.68 kPa, 7.17 kPa and 13.46 kPa, respectively

scope_conditions.measurement_method: tangent of curves in elastic zone

findings.antecedent: MFGO-5 lamella structure (maximum density 24.12 kg/m³) with highest GO loading
findings.consequent: acoustic absorption enhancement percentage across 128-4000 Hz vs Control-MF (26 ± 0.5 mm thickness)
findings.statement: MFGO-5 showed maximum ~60.3% enhancement in acoustic absorption across broad frequency range (1000-4000 Hz) compared to Control-MF
findings.quote: about 60 % enhancement in broad-band acoustic absorption (>100% at low frequencies) has been determined for this new structure
findings.mechanism: lamella structure dependent, not density dependent

findings.antecedent: Reduced-density MFGO samples (MFGO-3 and MFGO-5 after reduction process) vs non-reduced versions
findings.statement: Reduction process did not significantly change acoustic absorption peaks; values ranged 0.720 (MFGO-3) to 0.698 (MFrGO-3) and 0.787 (MFGO-5) to 0.771 (MFrGO-5)

sample.population: MFGO-3 and MFGO-5 samples before/after reduction

findings.quote: The change in acoustic activity over the broad frequency range from 128 Hz to 4000 Hz is also negligible, which is 0.720 for MFGO-3 sample to 0.698 for MFrGO-3 and 0.787 for MFGO-5 and 0.771 for MFrGO-5.

scope_conditions.process: reduction via hydrazine vapor + thermal annealing at 160°C

findings.mechanism: physical structure remains unchanged, density reduction does not alter acoustic absorption if microstructure is preserved

findings.antecedent: MFGO-5 lamella structure (24.12 kg/m³) vs Control-MF
findings.statement: MFGO-5 showed flow resistivity of approximately 40932 Ns/m³, about 4 times higher than Control-MF (~10450 Ns/m³)
findings.quote: measured flow resistivity of the highest density lamella structure (MFGO-5) was found approximately 40932 Ns/m³ which is about four times higher than that of Control-MF (~10450 Ns/m³)
findings.mechanism: GO-based lamella structures increase air-flow resistance and tortuosity

findings.antecedent: Initial Control-MF foam density vs after maximum GO loading into MFGO-5 structure
findings.statement: Control-MF initial density 9.84 kg/m³ increased to MFGO-5 density of 24.12 kg/m³ after maximum GO loading
findings.quote: The density of the initial Control-MF foam (9.84 kg/m³) was increased to 24.12 kg/m³, after a maximum GO loading in its unaffected structure.
findings.mechanism: incorporation of GO sheets increases material mass

findings.antecedent: MFGO-3 and MFrGO-3 (reduced) samples vs Control-MF for moisture absorption/desorption
findings.statement: MFGO and MFrGO samples showed 4-5 times better moisture insulation compared to Control-MF over 500 minute elapsed time
findings.quote: excellent moisture insulation that provided almost 4-5 times better moisture insulation compared to Control-MF
findings.mechanism: self-assembled GO lamella sheets create impermeable barrier layer to moisture penetration

findings.antecedent: MFGO-3 (non-reduced) vs MFrGO-3 (reduced) for water contact angle measurement
findings.statement: GO-incorporated melamine skeleton showed enhanced water contact angle initially (~104°), which became superhydrophobic (~155°) after reduction process
findings.quote: water contact angle of CA~104°, which further became superhydrophobic (super water repellent) showing a water contact angle of ~155° after the reduction process

scope_conditions.process: reduction via hydrazine vapor + thermal annealing

findings.mechanism: reduction of oxygen functional groups creates hydrophobic surface

findings.antecedent: MFGO-3 sample thermal stability (thermogravimetric analysis) vs MFGO-3 non-reduced and Control-MF
findings.consequent: mass loss temperature stages and residual mass after combustion
findings.statement: MFrGO-3 sample showed higher thermal stability with single mass loss step at 350°C, vs MFGO-3 with two mass loss steps between 150-400°C due to abundant oxygen functional groups
findings.quote: MFGO-3 sample lost mass in two stages between 150 °C and 400 °C, whereas only a single step mass loss was identified for MFrGO-3 sample at 350 °C
findings.mechanism: reduction of oxygen functional groups removes unstable decomposition pathways

findings.antecedent: Fire hazard testing: MFGO sample (MFrGO-3) vs unreduced GO sample (MFGO-3) and Control-MF exposed to gasoline flame (10 μl)
findings.statement: Reduced MFrGO-3 sample maintained structural integrity under fire exposure for extended time, showing fire-retardant properties. Unreduced MFGO showed explosive fire hazard; control showed rapid ignition
instruments_used: fire exposure test with gasoline flame
findings.quote: GO film was found to possess an explosive fire hazard due to its possible flammability... self-explosive behaviour of GO film was mitigated by reduction of MFGO lamella structure for enhanced stability

stimulus_description.duration: sequential frames at 0, 5, 15, 20, 30 seconds for Control; 0, 5, 10, 15, 20 seconds for MFGO/MFrGO

findings.mechanism: reduction of oxygen functional groups reduces flammability; structural integrity maintained by GO lamella

limitations: No statistical testing or significance levels reported
Limited sample sizes (typically n=1 per condition for acoustic measurements)
Single-thickness acoustic measurements at 26 mm (though thickness variation tested for MFGO-1)
No information on measurement uncertainty or standard deviations for most acoustic data
Fire testing appears qualitative (visual observation of char/combustion) rather than quantitative
No explicit control of temperature/humidity during acoustic testing
Human hearing sensitivity range primarily 1000-5000 Hz but broader 128-4000 Hz tested
overall_theory_links: Structure-property relationship: absorption is structure-dependent, not solely density-dependent
Tortuosity and air-flow resistance as primary mechanisms for acoustic absorption enhancement
Moisture insulation through barrier layer formation by self-assembled GO lamella
Thermal and fire-retardant properties through reduction of oxygen functional groups
